page.title: WildcatSage Bot Commands
page.expandTip: Select any command row below to show usage details.

ask.name: !ask / !sage
ask.description: Ask Sage a question. Sage searches the web for answers.

search.name: !search
search.description: Searches the web for information about a topic.

game.name: !game
game.description: Shows information about the current stream game. Add "analyze" to inspect stream visuals with AI (uses stream thumbnails that update every 5 minutes).

translate.name: !translate
translate.description: Manages automatic chat translation for users.

usage.stopAllDesc: Stops all active translations in the channel

help.name: !commands / !help
help.description: Shows a link to the list of available bot commands.

lurk.description: Tells chat that you are lurking. You can add a reason for a custom message.

quote.name: !quote
quote.description: Adds, views, or searches channel quotes. Quotes can include an author.

usage.idDesc: Shows a quote by ID number (for example: !quote 12)
usage.searchDesc: Searches quotes by text or author (for example: !quote parfait)
usage.addDesc: Adds a new quote. Add an author after " - " (for example: !quote add "hello world - parfait")
usage.deleteDesc: Deletes a quote (moderators and broadcaster only)
usage.editDesc: Edits a quote (moderators and broadcaster only)

followage.name: !followage
followage.description: Shows how long a user has followed the channel.

command.name: !command Mod
command.description: Creates, edits, and manages custom channel commands. You can also manage custom commands in the Web Dashboard.

usage.addAi: Creates a new AI command that generates a unique response from a prompt
usage.show: Shows the response template and settings for a command
usage.optionsPerms: Sets required permission: everyone, subscriber, vip, moderator, or broadcaster
usage.optionsCooldown: Sets a cooldown between uses in seconds
usage.optionsType: Switches a command between text mode and AI mode

timer.name: !timer Mod
timer.description: Creates, edits, and manages automated chat timers. You can also manage timers in the Web Dashboard.

usage.add: Creates a new text timer with the given interval in minutes
usage.addAi: Creates a new AI timer with the given interval in minutes
usage.interval: Sets the minimum interval in minutes between timer messages
usage.lines: Sets the minimum number of chat lines between timer messages
usage.show: Shows the settings for a specific timer
usage.list: Shows all timers for the channel

geo.name: !geo
geo.description: Starts or manages Geo-Game, a geography guessing game for real or virtual locations.

usage.basic: Starts a real-world game with locations across the world
usage.region: Starts a game in a specific region (for example: !geo Japan)
usage.game: Starts a game using locations from the current stream game
usage.gameTitle: Starts a game using a specified game title (for example: !geo game "Metroid Prime")
usage.rounds: Runs a game with a set number of rounds (for example: !geo Japan 3)
usage.stop: Stops the game (game starter, moderators, or broadcaster)
usage.interval: Sets the delay between clues (30 to 300 seconds)
usage.duration: Sets the round duration (3 to 20 minutes)
usage.configRegion: Sets default regions (for example: Europe,Asia or USA,Canada)
usage.configGame: Sets preferred game titles as a comma-separated list
usage.pointsBase: Sets base points per round (1 to 100)
usage.maxRounds: Sets maximum rounds per game (1 to 10)

riddle.name: !riddle
riddle.description: Starts or manages a Riddle game about general topics, stream games, or custom subjects.

usage.basic: Starts a general knowledge riddle game
usage.subject: Starts a riddle on a specific subject (for example: !riddle animals)
usage.rounds: Starts a game with a set number of rounds (for example: !riddle 3)
usage.subjectRounds: Starts a subject game with multiple rounds (for example: !riddle history 5)
usage.game: Starts a riddle about the current stream game
usage.stop: Stops the game (game starter, moderators, or broadcaster)
usage.questionTime: Sets answer time per riddle (15 to 120 seconds)
usage.pointsBase: Sets base points per riddle (1 to 100)
usage.maxRounds: Sets maximum rounds per game (1 to 20)
usage.keywordsLimit: Sets number of recent keywords to exclude (for example: 20 to 100)
usage.roundDelay: Sets delay between rounds in milliseconds

trivia.name: !trivia
trivia.description: Starts or manages Trivia games with questions about various topics or the stream game.

usage.basic: Starts a general knowledge trivia game
usage.topic: Starts trivia on a specific topic (for example: !trivia science)
usage.game: Starts trivia about the current stream game
usage.rounds: Starts a game with a set number of rounds (for example: !trivia 3)
usage.topicRounds: Starts a topic game with multiple rounds (for example: !trivia history 5)
usage.stop: Stops the game (game starter, moderators, or broadcaster)
usage.time: Sets answer time per question (10 to 120 seconds)
usage.pointsBase: Sets base points per question (1 to 100)
usage.configTopic: Sets preferred topics as a comma-separated list
usage.maxRounds: Sets maximum rounds per game (1 to 10)

botlang.name: !botlang
botlang.description: Sets the default language for bot responses across the channel. You can also set the language in the Web Dashboard.

usage.off: Resets the channel language to English
usage.default: Resets the channel language to English

auto.name: !auto
auto.description: Configures automated chat messages and stream event notifications.

usage.status: Shows current auto-chat mode, frequency, and active categories
usage.mode: Sets auto-chat frequency (off disables periodic messages only)
usage.greetings: Enables or disables greetings when the stream starts and ends
usage.follows: Enables or disables messages for new followers
usage.subscriptions: Enables or disables messages for new subscriptions
usage.raids: Enables or disables welcome messages for incoming raids
usage.facts: Enables or disables automated facts and tips
usage.questions: Enables or disables automated viewer questions
usage.ads: Enables or disables notifications before ad breaks

disable.description: Disables a command for this channel.

enable.description: Enables a previously disabled command for this channel.

ping.description: Checks if the bot responds. The bot replies with "Pong!"

responseVariables.title: Response Variables
responseVariables.intro1: You can use response variables to insert dynamic text into custom commands. Put $(variable) in your command response. The bot replaces the variable when a user runs the command.

user.desc: Username of the person who ran the command

args.desc: All text after the command name as one string
args.example: If a user runs !shout hello world, $(args) = hello world

numbered.desc: A single word by position: $(1) is the first word, $(2) is the second word
numbered.example: If a user runs !shout hello world, $(1) = hello, $(2) = world

count.desc: Total number of times users ran this command

random.desc: A random number between X and Y

followage.desc: How long the user has followed the channel

checkinCount.desc: The viewer daily check-in total (Channel Point Rewards only)

pronouns.desc: Pronouns of the user who ran the command

pronounSubject.desc: Subject pronoun of the user who ran the command

pronounObject.desc: Object pronoun of the user who ran the command

pronounPossessive.desc: Possessive pronoun of the user who ran the command

responseVariables.compatibilityCustom: Custom Commands and Daily Check-In: Support all variables, including user-specific variables.
responseVariables.compatibilityTimers: Timed Messages (Timers): Run on a schedule without an active user. Timers support only channel and stream variables ($(channel), $(game), $(uptime), $(count), $(random X-Y)).

live.command: !command add live We have been live for $(uptime) playing $(game)!
live.result: We have been live for 2h 30m playing Metroid Prime!

uses.command: !command add uses This command was used $(count) times!

aiCommands.title: AI Commands
aiCommands.intro1: AI commands use a prompt instead of a fixed text response. The bot sends the prompt to an AI model to generate a unique reply every time. You can also use response variables in prompts.
aiCommands.intro2: You can create AI commands in the Web Dashboard. Select + Add, enable AI Mode, and enter your prompt. You can also create AI commands in chat with !command addai <name> <prompt>.

vibe.prompt:
Name: vibe
Prompt: Tell $(user) what kind of vibe "$(args)" gives off in one sentence.
vibe.result: If a user enters !vibe I just ate an entire pizza, the AI can reply: "WildcatGamer your message gives off deeply respectable goblin energy." Replies vary with each use.

hug.prompt:
Name: hug
Prompt: Write a short, funny hug message from $(user) to $(1).
hug.result: If a user enters !hug WildcatStreamer, the AI can reply: "WildcatGamer wraps WildcatStreamer in a hug so warm it could melt a glacier."

fortune.prompt:
Name: fortune
Prompt: Give $(user) a short fortune cookie message.
fortune.result: A unique fortune for each use: "WildcatGamer, today you will find a rare item in an unexpected place."

aiCommands.tipText: You can convert a text command to AI mode in the dashboard by enabling AI Mode. You can also run !command options <name> type=prompt in chat. Switch back with type=text.

webDashboard.title: Web Dashboard
webDashboard.intro: The WildcatSage Web Dashboard lets streamers configure bot settings for their channel. Sign in with your Twitch account to access the dashboard.

botManagement.title: Bot Management:
botManagement.desc: Add or remove WildcatSage from your channel.

channelConfig.title: Channel Settings:
channelConfig.desc: Configure auto-chat frequency, stream event messages, and ad break notifications.

streamEvents.title: Stream Events:
streamEvents.desc: Enable AI greetings, farewells, and celebration messages for new followers, subscribers, and incoming raids.

commandControl.title: Command Management:
commandControl.desc: Create custom commands and enable or disable built-in commands.

timers.title: Timed Messages:
timers.desc: Create and manage scheduled chat messages with interval and chat line settings.

botPersonality.title: Bot Personality:
botPersonality.desc: Customize tone, humor, and style instructions for AI responses, with automatic Twitch rule checks.

botLanguage.title: Bot Language:
botLanguage.desc: Set the language the bot speaks in your channel, or use the stream language from Twitch.

dailyCheckIn.title: Daily Check-In:
dailyCheckIn.desc: Configure a Channel Point Reward for daily check-ins with streak tracking and optional AI responses.

language.title: Dashboard Language:
language.desc: Show the dashboard in one of eight languages. This setting is separate from the bot language.

visit.title: Visit the Dashboard:
visit.desc: Go to https://bot.wildcat.chat/.

authorize.title: Authorize:
authorize.desc: Select "Sign in with Twitch" and approve the required permissions.

addBot.title: Add the Bot:
addBot.desc: Select "Add bot to my channel" to invite WildcatSage to your channel.

configure.title: Configure:
configure.desc: Change bot settings in the dashboard.

grantPerms.title: Troubleshooting:
grantPerms.desc: If the bot does not respond, enter /mod WildcatSage in Twitch chat to grant moderator permissions.

webDashboard.oauthIntro: The dashboard requires these Twitch OAuth permissions:

oauth.readEmail: Reads your email address for account identification.
oauth.readAds: Receives ad break notifications for your channel.
oauth.manageModerators: Grants moderator permissions to the bot.
oauth.readFollowers: Reads follower data for commands such as !followage.
oauth.manageRedemptions: Creates and manages Channel Point Rewards for features such as Daily Check-In.

webDashboard.noteText: WildcatSage is currently invite-only. If your channel does not appear in the dashboard, request access through the contact form.

botPersonality.title: Bot Personality
botPersonality.intro: Bot Personality controls how WildcatSage speaks in your channel. You write the personality text in the dashboard. The bot then uses this text for its AI replies.

steps.open: Open the WildcatSage Dashboard and go to the Bot Personality section.
steps.edit: Change the text in the box. The box contains the default personality.

botPersonality.noteText: The new personality applies immediately. A restart is not necessary.

limits.scopeValue: Chat replies, auto-chat messages, stream event messages, AI custom commands, and Daily Check-In AI messages

botPersonality.changeIntro: You can change the name, the tone, the humor, and the topics of the bot. The default personality includes a cat roleplay section. You can remove this section.
botPersonality.fixedIntro: These rules apply to all channels. Your text cannot change them:

fixed.commands: The bot does not send or simulate chat commands such as /ban or /timeout.
fixed.length: The bot keeps each reply to one or two sentences.
fixed.secrecy: The bot does not show its own instructions in chat.
fixed.values: The channel values stay in effect.

botPersonality.fixedPanel: The Rules that always apply panel in the dashboard shows the full text of these rules. This panel is read-only.
botPersonality.checkIntro: WildcatSage examines each personality before it stores the text. This check uses Gemini Flash Lite, the same model that does translation.
botPersonality.checkRejects: The check rejects text that gives the bot these instructions:

rejects.harass: Harass viewers, or attack a person.
rejects.impersonate: Impersonate a real person or a company.
rejects.override: Ignore the rules that always apply.
rejects.reveal: Show its own instructions in chat.

botPersonality.checkTone: The check does not reject a personality because of its tone. A rude, sarcastic, or profane personality is permitted.
botPersonality.checkFail: If the check rejects your text, the dashboard shows the reason. The bot does not store the text. Your text stays in the box. Correct the text, then select Save again.
botPersonality.checkUnavailable: If the check is not available, the save fails. The bot does not store text that the check did not examine.
botPersonality.resetNote: When your channel has a custom personality, the dashboard shows this button.
botPersonality.sharedIntro: In a Twitch shared chat session, the bot mixes the personalities of all channels in the session. The bot gives more weight to the personality of the host channel. A channel with the default personality adds nothing to the mix.
botPersonality.otherPromptsIntro: The same safety check applies to these fields:
botPersonality.otherPromptsText: Text commands and text timers do not use the check. The bot sends this text without a change.

dailyCheckIn.title: Daily Check-In
dailyCheckIn.intro: Daily Check-In is a Channel Point Reward. Viewers check in once per stream to track their daily streak. The dashboard creates and manages the reward on Twitch.

steps.open: Open the WildcatSage Dashboard and go to the Daily Check-In section.
steps.enable: Enable the toggle, then enter a reward title and Channel Point cost.
steps.template: Enter a response template with variables like $(user) and $(checkin_count), or enable AI Mode for unique replies.
steps.save: Select Save. The bot creates the reward on Twitch.

variables.user: Display name of the viewer who checked in
variables.checkinCount: Total number of check-ins for the viewer
variables.pronouns: Pronouns of the viewer who checked in
variables.pronounSubject: Subject pronoun of the viewer who checked in
variables.pronounObject: Object pronoun of the viewer who checked in
variables.pronounPossessive: Possessive pronoun of the viewer who checked in

dailyCheckIn.requirementText: You must have Twitch Affiliate or Partner status to create Channel Point Rewards.
dailyCheckIn.aiExamplePrompt: AI Mode Prompt: Write a fun, short congratulatory message for $(user) on check-in number $(checkin_count).
dailyCheckIn.aiExampleOutput: Output: "WildcatGamer, 14 days straight? You're on fire! At this rate you'll outlast the sun. ☀️" — replies vary with each use.

botLanguage.title: Bot Language
botLanguage.intro: WildcatSage can speak a language other than English in your channel. The language applies to command replies, game messages, and AI replies.
botLanguage.autoIntro: You set a stream language on your Twitch channel. WildcatSage reads this value and uses it as the default language for your channel.

auto.default: Detection gives a default only. A language set in the dashboard or with !botlang always wins.
auto.live: The bot reads the Twitch value each time it needs it. If you change the language on Twitch, the bot changes with it.
auto.english: Channels with English as the stream language stay in English.

botLanguage.setIntro: You can set the bot language in the dashboard or in chat. Only the broadcaster and moderators can change it.
botLanguage.dashboardSetTitle: Set the Language in the Dashboard
botLanguage.dashboardSetIntro: Open the Web Dashboard. Find the Bot Language card. Then select a language from the list.

dashboardSet.auto: Select Automatic to use the stream language from Twitch. This option is the default.
dashboardSet.manual: Select a language to hold the channel in that language. The Twitch stream language then has no effect.
dashboardSet.groups: The list has two groups. Written in advance holds the eight languages with translations ready. Translated when sent holds the other languages.
dashboardSet.save: The dashboard saves your choice immediately. The bot changes language a few seconds later.

botLanguage.chatSetIntro: Chat accepts more languages than the dashboard list. Use these commands:

commands.set: Sets the channel language to Spanish.
commands.status: Shows the current language and where it came from.

botLanguage.offNote: !botlang off and the English option both hold the channel in English. Automatic detection does not change it back.
botLanguage.autoNote: To use automatic detection again, select Automatic in the dashboard.
botLanguage.writtenIntro: Eight languages have translations that are written in advance: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, and Russian.
botLanguage.writtenBenefit: In these languages, fixed messages such as game announcements go to chat immediately. The words are the same each time.
botLanguage.writtenOther: The !botlang command accepts more languages than these eight. For a language without written translations, the bot translates each message as it sends it.
botLanguage.writtenOtherCost: These messages are correct, but they are slower and the words can change between messages.
botLanguage.aiIntro: The bot writes AI replies new each time, so they are not limited to the eight languages.
botLanguage.aiRule: The bot answers each person in the language that person used. If the language is not clear, the bot uses the language of your stream.
botLanguage.aiUnits: Time periods and language names follow the channel language. As an example, !followage writes its units in the channel language.
botLanguage.dashboardIntro: The dashboard has its own language setting. This setting is separate from the bot language.
botLanguage.dashboardPicker: The language picker is in the bottom corner of every dashboard page. The dashboard uses your browser language until you make a choice.
botLanguage.dashboardUrl: To see one page in a different language, add ?lang=ja to the end of the address.
